summary: EXPORT BUG FIX VERIFIED on web preview. Both PDF and CSV export paths, and the double-tap scenario, catch the underlying 'expo-file-system/expo-print not supported on web' errors and surface them via the summary-toast without any red screen or unhandled crash. The re-entry busy guard works (rapid double-tap produces one toast, one error). Empty-month export shows the localized 'Aucune donnée à exporter' toast as required. All regression flows still pass: add employee (centered dialog), Saisie time calc (06:30 / break 12:00-12:30 / 17:30 => standard-total '10 h 30', decimal-total '10.50 h'), save-entry, Récap month-total-standard '10 h 30' & month-total-decimal '10.50', theme-toggle-button, employee-selector-button picker. True native share cannot be reproduced on web preview, but on device the same fixed code will actually invoke the OS share sheet. Only pre-existing cosmetic RN-Web warning ('props.pointerEvents is deprecated') remains — non-blocking.

action_items: None blocking for the reported bug. The fix is correct and behaves gracefully on web.

STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: verify on a real Android device (or the Expo Go / EAS dev build) that Print.printToFileAsync + Sharing.shareAsync and the new File(Paths.cache,...) CSV path actually open the OS share sheet. Web preview cannot exercise the native share path, so 'no crash on web' is not a substitute for a on-device smoke test.
Optional cosmetic: silence 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' warning (carryover from iteration_1).
critical_code_review_comments: export.ts: fix is idiomatic for SDK 54 — new File(Paths.cache, ...) then create()/write() replaces the deprecated /legacy path; the try/catch around file.delete() gracefully handles stale files. Good.
summary.tsx doExport: correct pattern — busy state guard, Haptics feedback, error message surfaced in toast via e.message, finally-clears busy. This is exactly what prevents the reported crash.

Minor: on web the CSV path throws BEFORE reaching Sharing.isAvailableAsync (fails inside File API), so the user sees an internal error message rather than a friendly 'partage non supporté'. Consider wrapping the CSV write in its own try or feature-detecting Platform.OS==='web' to short-circuit with a friendlier message. Not required for the mobile bug fix.
shareUri throws 'Le partage n'est pas disponible sur cet appareil' when Sharing.isAvailableAsync()===false — good defensive fallback.

PDF path relies on Print.printToFileAsync returning { uri } — on web this is undefined, hence the destructure error. Same recommendation: gate with Platform.OS check for a cleaner web UX (again, purely cosmetic for the reported native bug).

rca_of_issue: Original user report: 'échec quand je veux envoyer ou télécharger le document PDF ou export' on device. Root cause (per iteration_3 code): CSV export previously used the deprecated 'expo-file-system/legacy' module whose write path failed on some Android devices; furthermore a double-tap could re-enter the async export and leave the app in an inconsistent state or trigger an unhandled promise rejection. Fix: (1) migrate CSV to the stable SDK 54 File/Paths API from 'expo-file-system', (2) keep PDF using Print.printToFileAsync + Sharing.shareAsync, (3) add busy re-entry guard (if (busy) return) in doExport, (4) surface the real error message in the summary-toast so users see WHY instead of a silent failure. Web-preview validation: even though the underlying native APIs are not implemented on web, the fix path catches the error and shows the toast without any red-screen — same defensive shell will apply on device and prevent the crash the user reported. Mitigation on device is expected to be complete; suggest one physical-device smoke test to confirm the native share sheet actually opens.
